summary.headline: Advanced Enzyme Q1 FY27 revenue rose 2% YoY to INR 1,898 million, but EBITDA fell 10% to INR 510 million as margin dropped to 27%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR 1,898 million grew 2% YoY but fell 7% QoQ, held back by an extra INR 100 million sales reversal for export shipments still in transit. EBITDA declined 10% YoY and 19% QoQ to INR 510 million, with margin at 27% versus 30% a year ago, attributed to lower realisation, higher power and fuel costs, and a sales-mix shift. PAT was INR 386 million, down 5% YoY. Management guided to a return to about 30-32% EBITDA margin, double-digit growth for the rest of the year, and announced a INR 697 million buyback and full acquisition of JC Biotech.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 120-130 crore capex to be spent in FY27 and what is the growth component?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed INR 123 crore for FY27, about INR 20 crore may slip to Q2; about INR 20 crore maintenance, INR 50 crore R&D facility, balance growth. Fermentation utilisation is around 70-75%, with a capacity decision next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is US growth lagging the market, and what is the reason for the about 14% decline in international Human Nutrition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a weak US environment, the shift to branding most ingredients (which takes time), geopolitical issues, tariffs and hiring challenges; expects US growth of 8-10% at most at this juncture.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 growth reach 12%+ given the sales reversal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, it expects double-digit growth in the balance three quarters; the INR 10 crore incremental reversal (about 8% drag) is expected to come back in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Will the sales reversal normalise, and what caused it?
qa_highlights.answer: Export shipments were booked but still in transit at quarter end, so revenue was not recognised; the incremental reversal was INR 100 million over normal quarterly reversals and has already been recorded as of the call date.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30% EBITDA margin achievable, and will energy costs ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to return to about 30% and cited 30-32% as the target, with energy costs easing from Q2 through operational efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of novel food approval and the EFSA process?
qa_highlights.answer: Still under EFSA consideration; management said it could take three to six months, depending on authorities, and the process is on and off.

qa_highlights.question: Which new products and markets are driving future growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not track product-level sales; 15-20 molecules are in the pipeline, with expansion into biocatalysis, animal feed, ruminant, food, baking and detergent; bioenergy has no revenue yet and is deferred to after the new R&D facility next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital position at June 30, 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory about INR 190 crore, receivables about INR 131 crore, payables about INR 41 crore, net working capital about INR 280 crore; working capital cycle about 125-138 days.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA margin to return to about 30% for the full year, with 30-32% EBITDA margin cited as the target range for the rest of FY27.
Double-digit revenue growth expected for the balance three quarters of FY27; management says the Q1 INR 100 million incremental sales reversal (about 8% growth drag) should reverse in Q2.
Margin recovery expected from lower power and fuel costs and operational efficiency from Q2 onward.
US business guided to about 8-10% growth at current juncture; management said about 8% by year-end, and US is not expected to exceed 8-10% near term.
Biocatalysis expected to deliver good growth in H2 FY27.
Management said it expects progressive momentum as the year advances and asked shareholders to assess the business on an annual horizon.
capex_capacity: Management confirmed INR 123 crore capex plan (as discussed at AGM) to be spent in FY27; about INR 20 crore may slip into Q2 FY27, mainly at a subsidiary.

Of the INR 123 crore: about INR 20 crore normal/maintenance capex, about INR 50 crore for R&D facility already under work in progress (expected functional in the next quarter or so), balance growth capex; not segment-specific.
Fermentation capacity utilisation is about 70-75% (vs the 55-60% the company historically cited); management will decide in the next quarter on starting capacity-expansion capex.
New R&D facility expected next year; JC Biotech facility is capacity-constrained for solvent handling and capacity is being increased.
demand_pricing: Revenue INR 1,898 million; Human Healthcare down 7% YoY on lower Pharma API sales; India sales INR 580 million (vs INR 699 million in Q4, INR 659 million a year ago); international INR 559 million (vs INR 582 million in Q4, INR 552 million a year ago).
International Human Nutrition declined about 14% in the quarter; management attributed this to US business shift toward branding of ingredients, geopolitical issues, tariffs and hiring challenges.
Pricing: management said realisation is better than Q4 and Q1 FY26 because some prices were increased; declined to quantify competitive pricing pressure on the largest product.
Top 10 customers about 23% of revenue (27% a year ago); top 10 products about 45% (49% in Q4 FY26). Management said 70-80% of customers are constant and 20-30% of business changes each period.
Specialized Manufacturing up 41% YoY; Bioprocessing up 30% YoY on Food business; Animal Healthcare down 3% YoY.
Europe (evoxx) revenue INR 74 million, growth mainly from food area per management. SciTech revenue INR 201 million vs INR 145 million a year ago.
Serratiopeptidase: management declined to disclose quarterly number; said a reported ban would have no meaningful impact (about 1%) given the FDC combination.
Protein hydrolysis products began generating sales in the quarter; sugar-management patent (Alternansucrase) granted in the US.
risks_watch: US business: growth stalled, branding transition and geopolitical/tariff headwinds; management gave no quantified new-product plan for US.
Margin: power and fuel costs elevated; FY27 30% EBITDA target depends on cost normalisation from Q2.
Revenue timing: INR 100 million extra export reversal shows dependence on shipment timing; Q2 must show reversal and double-digit growth.
Product concentration: serratiopeptidase dependence is high; regulatory/ban news flagged, though management says impact is about 1%.
Pricing and competition on the largest product: management declined to quantify realisation changes.
Capacity: utilisation at 70-75% triggers a capex decision next quarter; watch for capex commitments beyond INR 123 crore.
Governance/disclosure: management declined to disclose serratiopeptidase numbers, Starya Labs is not yet operational, and inventory and several questions were deferred.
key_quotes: Our fundamentals remain strong, execution continues to be solid, and we are well positioned to capitalize on growth opportunities.
We remain confident in delivering sustainable revenue growth consistent with our annual guidance.
As of now, we think we should be able to grow in double digits.
Yes. We expect that it shall come back to the normal level of about 30% of EBITDA.
summary.management_tone: Cautious and defensive: management described Q1 as soft and muted, blamed geopolitics, energy costs and US business changes, and repeatedly deflected QoQ and product-level questions while keeping FY27 guidance of double-digit growth and about 30% margin.
